text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Initiative to move elections up; Yisrael Ba'Aliya and Third Way parties checking possibility; Yisrael Ba'Aliya head Sharansky says he'd consider positively proposals for early elections.
- Feelers to set up new party with Meridor; Meridor: Netanyahu is not fit to be prime minister.
- Chances lessen that Infrastructure Minister Sharon will go to Finance Ministry.
- Senior Likud party figures: the next target (of Prime Minister Netanyahu) is Defence Minister Mordechai.
MAARIV
- Cabinet shuffle awaits return of former justice minister Neeman from abroad, then it will be decided.
- In wake of economic reform plan: interest lowered 1.2 percent, sharp stock rise, buy orders for foreign currency.
GLOBES
- Sharon leading candidate for Finance Minister.
- Economically, Meridor's resignation was unnecessary.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli team meets Egypt's peace envoy in Cairo.
- Netanyahu approves conversion bill compromise.
- Netanyahu weighs cabinet options; in no rush to replace Meridor.
- Q1 jobless rate at 7.3 percent.
- Optisystems raises $15 million in Wall Street IPO.
HAARETZ
- Sharon and Neeman candidates to replace resigning Finance Minister Meridor.
- Reform rabbi marries two Lesbians in Tel Aviv.
